items.evidence: After `page.reload()`, `nameInput` is checked with `toHaveValue(NEW_NAME)` and the header title with `toHaveText(NEW_NAME)` (diff lines 75-78). Both would fail if the save mutation never ran.
Criterion 1, the title after saving, is asserted at diff line 70. Criterion 2, the name field and title after a reload, is asserted at diff lines 77-78.
`e2e/pages/`, `e2e/lib/` and `e2e/scenarios/` have no product-page or products-list object, so nothing is duplicated. The spec reuses `PRODUCTS` and `ORDERS_SCENARIO`.
There is no `waitForTimeout`, no sleep and no fixed-delay polling.
`test` and `expect` come from `../../fixtures/test.ts` (diff line 9). The test is not tagged `parallel()` and writes nothing to the cache or the dumps.

e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts diff lines 42-51 (spec lines 35-44): the row is found by the generated, positional id `#glide-cell-1-0` and opened by hovering at hard-coded pixel offsets for the first row, where text-filtering the grid (as the legacy `gridCanvas.getByText` pattern did) would work. The grid itself is found with a CSS attribute selector (diff line 35).
The spec uses the orders scenario's existing E2E Hoodie and only navigates to it. It creates no data through the API or the UI.
There are no hard-coded ids. The product name comes from `PRODUCTS.hoodie.name`, and the product URL is captured at runtime.
The spec signs in as the default `admin` actor through the fixture, which suits a ticket that names no permission. There is no UI login and no credentials in the spec.
The spec is under `e2e/tests/products/`, and `typecheck.txt` reports exit 0 with no errors.

e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts diff lines 31-36 and 39-53: every locator (header, nameInput, saveButton, notifications, grid, rowAnchor) and the multi-step search-and-open flow are written inline in the spec instead of on a page object.
No page-object members are added, so this does not apply.
`// Arrange`, `// Act` and `// Assert` comments are present (diff lines 29, 60, 67).
e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts diff lines 38-79: the test has four stages (open, rename, check after save, check after reload), marked by numbered comments instead of `test.step`.
"Rename a product #e2e" (diff line 28) names the behaviour and carries the `#e2e` tag.
The JSDoc header (diff lines 12-18) says what the spec covers and explains the grid-anchor approach.
All assertions are web-first. `boundingBox()` is read only to position the mouse, not asserted on.
e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts diff line 41: the URL assertion `/query=E2E%20Hoodie/` types in the product name instead of deriving it from `PRODUCTS.hoodie.name`.
There is no cleanup and no unique or timestamped names.
There are no per-test timeouts, retries, `networkidle` or `waitForLoadState`.
Relative imports keep the `.ts` extension, and nothing is imported from `@playwright/test`.
There is no `any`, no cast and no untyped `gql` call.

e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts diff lines 7-8, 38, 61, 68, 74: generator boilerplate (`// spec: ...`, `// seed: ...`) and numbered step comments that restate the next lines instead of explaining why.

structured_output.summary: The test proves the rename: it reads the name back after a reload, covers both acceptance criteria, uses the orders scenario and the suite fixture, and type-checks. It fails one blocker, B6: it opens the row through the generated positional id `#glide-cell-1-0`, hard-coded pixel offsets for the first row, and a CSS attribute selector for the grid. It also fails five minors: locators and the open flow are inline instead of on a page object (M1); the stages are not `test.step`s (M4); the URL check types in the product name instead of using `PRODUCTS.hoodie.name` (M8); and generator boilerplate and step-narrating comments remain (M13).
